title: The calf of gold
hook: while Musa is on the mountain the people make a golden calf, and Harun tries to hold them
carry: wait for the one who's coming back
tomorrow: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon

segments.voice: Yesterday: the sea, and one sentence at the water's edge. Your line was my lord is with me. Did you say it in a tight spot? Day fifty-four, the last of our two weeks with Musa.

You know how fast things slip when the person holding them together steps out. The teacher leaves the room for five minutes. The parent goes on a work trip. The manager takes a vacation, and by Thursday nobody's following the plan. The people have just walked through the sea on dry ground. They've seen Pharaoh's army drown. And Musa goes up the mountain to meet his Lord, and leaves his brother Harun in charge. He's gone forty nights. And in that time, a man called the Samiri gathers up their gold jewelry, melts it down, and makes something. Today: the calf of gold.
screen: `WHEN THE LEADER STEPS OUT.` → `FORTY NIGHTS ON THE MOUNTAIN.` → `THE GOLD IS MELTED DOWN.`

segments.voice: Surah Ta-Ha. The Samiri brings out a calf, a body that makes a lowing sound, and says: this is your god, and the god of Musa, but he forgot. Harun, in the Qur'an, doesn't go along with it. He stands up and says: my people, you're only being tested by this. Your Lord is the Most Merciful. So follow me and obey my command. And their answer is the saddest line in the story: we will not stop devoting ourselves to it until Musa comes back to us. Hear that? They said they were waiting for Musa. And while they waited, they made a calf. They filled the empty time with something they could see and touch. Musa comes down angry and grieved. He grabs his brother by the beard and head: what stopped you, when you saw them going astray? And Harun says: son of my mother, don't seize my beard or my head. I was afraid you'd say I had split the Children of Israel. He'd held on as best he could without tearing the people in two. Then Musa turns to the Samiri, and the calf is burned and scattered into the sea. Who the Samiri was, the Qur'an doesn't say, and scholars have offered many answers. That's the end of our two weeks with Musa. A chest on the river. Asiya's arms. His mother's cooled eye. A blow and a flight. Water at Madyan. Fire on the mountain. The staff. A loosened tongue. A gentle word. The magicians. The sea. And a calf made by people who couldn't wait.
screen: `A BODY THAT LOWS.` · `HARUN: YOU ARE BEING TESTED.` · `UNTIL MUSA COMES BACK TO US.` · `SON OF MY MOTHER.` · then, large: `WAIT FOR THE ONE COMING BACK.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice what you'd make into a calf. Settle, and breathe. When you're waiting, for news, for an answer, for someone to come back, what do you fill the time with? The phone. Food. Work. Shopping. Worrying, which can be its own golden calf. Don't judge it. Just find the thing you reach for when the waiting gets long, and look at it honestly for a moment. Then sit in the waiting itself, empty-handed, for the rest of the bell. If you pray, you can ask for patience in the gap. The bell holds the time.
The calf of gold. What the people made while they said they were waiting for Musa. Today's word.
Your line: wait for the one who's coming back. Today, in one long wait, try leaving the gap empty instead of filling it. Tomorrow, a new story: a boy, a dream, and eleven stars. Day fifty-four.

screen: `DAY 54 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ELEVEN STARS, THE SUN AND THE MOON.`

howItsDone: Muslims honor Harun as a prophet and brother of Musa, and the story of the calf is taught as a warning against filling a spiritual gap with something made by hand; it is told in several surahs.

fork.setup: you're Harun, left in charge. the people are gathering around a golden calf that makes a lowing sound. what do you do?
options: join them to keep the peace.
warn them: you're only being tested. follow me.
leave and go find Musa on the mountain.
fork.reveal: Harun warned them. they refused until Musa came back. later he told Musa he'd feared splitting the people apart.

original.note: Arabic: calf — the golden calf of Qur'an 20:88.

trapdoor: what you thought: people who worshipped a statue.
what it means: people who said they were waiting for Musa filled the waiting with something they could see, while Harun tried to hold them.
what a scholar hears: 20:88 calls it a jasad, a body, lahu khuwar, with a lowing sound; the Qur'an's Harun resists the calf, and the Samiri's identity is debated.

notes: All Qur'anic lines paraphrased, not quoted. 'This is your god, and the god of Musa, but he forgot' (20:88): commentators differ on who 'forgot' refers to (Musa, or the Samiri forgetting); the script keeps the ambiguity by quoting the claim as the Samiri's.
'Our last day with Musa' refers to this part of the path (days 43–54); Musa appears again later in the curriculum. Confirm.
Musa's anger and seizing Harun (20:92–94) described plainly; confirm tone.
The index title and practice kept; the look-back names the part's days 43–53.
Closing teaser mentions Yusuf's dream without teaching it.
